newsitem.title: PERU: Peru, Shell/Mobil sign oil exploration contract.
newsitem.headline: Peru, Shell/Mobil sign oil exploration contract.

text.p: Peru signed a contract with a consortium of oil giants Royal Dutch/Shell and Mobil to explore and develop oil Block 75 in Peru's jungle.

The oil block lies across the borders of the four counties of Ucayali, Junin, Madre de Dios and Cuzco in central and southern Peru, according to a decree published Sunday in official daily El Peruano. The decree gave no details about the block's size or estimated reserves.

Shell Prospecting and Development (Peru) B.V. and Mobil Exploration and Producing Peru Inc are the subsidiaries of the two oil giants that will carry out the exploration work in block 75, according to the decree.
The government has said it estimates its oil contracts require an investment of around $40 million.

For a contract signed last May, Shell and Mobil also formed a consortium to explore the huge oil gas reserves of the Camisea fields in the same region. Camisea is Peru's largest hydrocarbon project, which is expected to last 40 years and become the largest foreign investment commitment in Peru at up to an estimated $3.0 billion.

State oil licensing agent Perupetro now has 37 current oil contracts with private companies. Since it started offering the licenses four years ago, 15 have started producing oil, while 22 are at the exploration stage.

Perupetro is negotiating five more exploration and development contracts with Coastal and Atlantic Richfield Company ; Argentina's Pluspetrol; Britain's Enterprise Oil, and Peru's Buenaventura Ingenieros, according to the Energy and Mines ministry.
